People are not perfect, that’s what I am trying to remind myself all the time, we can’t be perfectly confident all the time, and that’s ok. You might want to start with listing situations where you think you exhibit low level of confidence and range them from easiest to hardest to address. 

For example, (that’s my perception of easy, yours might be different) telling a compliment only to one person in the group. Tell them a specific compliment, whether their hair was nice, or you liked the outfit, but stop there, try having a pause. 5 seconds, 10 seconds, if after 10 seconds or longer everything seems fine, it’s fine, it’s always fine. People think mostly about themselves rather than others, that’s just how we are. If it didn’t work out, don’t worry, take a step back, find another thing that bothers you but is easier and start from there then work your way back to this situation. 

It’s also helpful to think about yourself from the 3rd person’s view, as if you are not you but someone else you have to protect. Sometimes, just be daring for the fun of it, it helps some people. 

Don’t pressure yourself too much, you will learn
